subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 30, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - August 30, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS Community,

We're excited to share the latest updates from the AcreetionOS project. As always, we're committed to providing a community-driven, user-friendly Linux distribution based on Arch Linux, with a focus on privacy and no telemetry.

In recent news, the Debian community has voted to allow the responsible use of generative AI, a move that could have significant implications for the development of AI-powered tools in the Linux ecosystem. Meanwhile, Konstantin Ryabitsev has written a thought-provoking blog post about the impact of AI crawlers on the Linux community.

On the AcreetionOS front, we've been busy with various development activities. Our team has been working on improving the performance of our KIO (Kernel I/O) system, which is a crucial component of our distribution. We're also making progress on our Calamares installer, ensuring that users have a seamless experience when setting up their AcreetionOS systems.

In terms of code commits, we've had several updates to our GitHub repository, including a new newsletter and archive system, as well as improvements to our wiki guides. We've also made some tweaks to our CI/CD pipelines to ensure that our releases are smooth and efficient.

One notable commit was the addition of Firefox-UBlock-Origin to our Xlibre build, which should improve the overall browsing experience for our users. We've also re-triggered our GitLab mirror to ensure that our code is up-to-date and easily accessible.

In addition to these technical updates, we've been working on improving our community engagement. We're excited to announce that we'll be hosting a series of community meetups in the coming weeks, where we'll be discussing various topics related to Linux, development, and community building.

We're also proud to announce that our community has grown significantly, with new members joining our Discord server and contributing to our GitHub repository. We're grateful for the enthusiasm and support of our community, and we look forward to seeing what the future holds for AcreetionOS.

As always, we're committed to transparency and openness in our development process. We encourage our community to participate in our decision-making processes and provide feedback on our projects.

In closing, we'd like to thank our community for their continued support and enthusiasm. We're excited to see what the future holds for AcreetionOS, and we look forward to continuing to work together to build a better, more private, and more user-friendly Linux distribution.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift, Co-Lead Developers of AcreetionOS
